## Chapter Map {#chapter-map .section-title}

```{=html}
<div class="wh-book-grid wh-reveal">
  <article class="wh-book-card">
    <span class="wh-book-card__status">Ch 1</span>
    <div class="wh-book-card__title"><a href="./01-geometry-measurement.html">Geometry and measurement</a></div>
    <div class="wh-book-card__desc">Quantifying physical space. Perimeter, area, volume, and the coordinate geometry that lets you describe any shape with numbers.</div>
  </article>
  <article class="wh-book-card">
    <span class="wh-book-card__status">Ch 2</span>
    <div class="wh-book-card__title"><a href="./02-trigonometry.html">Trigonometry</a></div>
    <div class="wh-book-card__desc">Relating angles to side lengths. Sine, cosine, and tangent as ratios — and how a right triangle connects every angle to a ratio you can calculate.</div>
  </article>
  <article class="wh-book-card">
    <span class="wh-book-card__status">Ch 3</span>
    <div class="wh-book-card__title"><a href="./03-polynomials-factoring.html">Polynomials and factoring</a></div>
    <div class="wh-book-card__desc">Deconstructing complex equations. Polynomials as sums of power terms, factoring as reverse multiplication, and the quadratic formula as a shortcut.</div>
  </article>
  <article class="wh-book-card">
    <span class="wh-book-card__status">Ch 4</span>
    <div class="wh-book-card__title"><a href="./04-functions-relations.html">Functions and relations</a></div>
    <div class="wh-book-card__desc">Mapping inputs to outputs. The formal definition of a function, domain and range, composition, and what it means for a function to be invertible.</div>
  </article>
  <article class="wh-book-card">
    <span class="wh-book-card__status">Ch 5</span>
    <div class="wh-book-card__title"><a href="./05-boolean-logic.html">Boolean algebra and logic circuits</a></div>
    <div class="wh-book-card__desc">The algebra of true and false. AND, OR, NOT as operations — and how the same algebraic rules that govern numbers also govern logic and digital circuits.</div>
  </article>
</div>
```
